cards.title: Convert giveaway non-winners through a consolation offer
cards.summary: When running social giveaways, DM all non-winning entrants with an acknowledging message and an exclusive discount to convert disappointment into purchase.
cards.use_when: You are running a social media giveaway and planning the follow-up with people who did not win.

cards.title: Sequence operational fixes before scaling wild bets
cards.summary: A wild bet cannot rescue a relationship after a high-effort failure — fix operations and earn the right to be delightful first.
cards.use_when: You are planning your quarterly retention roadmap and deciding how to sequence customer support improvements versus delight campaigns.

cards.title: Instrument the right metric for each retention play
cards.summary: Match the metric to the play — CES, first-contact resolution and resolution time for support; LTV, earned media value, NPS and repurchase for delight wild bets.
cards.use_when: You are setting up reporting for a retention program and choosing KPIs.

cards.title: Match wild-bet tactics to their psychological driver
cards.summary: Choose the retention wild bet based on the driver you need — reciprocity, inner-circle advocacy, extreme personalization, trust generation, tribalism or buyer's-remorse mitigation.
cards.use_when: You are selecting which unconventional retention tactic to pilot and need to match the mechanism to a business problem.

cards.title: Design testable bundles without breaking the retention play
cards.summary: Apply the source's retention wild-bet principles through testable product and subscription bundle structures that balance trust, cadence and perceived value.
cards.use_when: You are building bundle or subscription SKUs and want to embed retention mechanics (pause flexibility, cadence control, artifact bonuses) into the offer rather than bolt them on.

cards.title: Track earned attention separately from incremental sales and campaign cost
cards.summary: Wild bets are not direct-response spend — their expected return shows up as earned media, organic referrals and UGC rather than attributable revenue in the campaign window.
cards.use_when: You are building the business case to leadership for an unscalable retention or brand spend that fails direct-attribution tests.

cards.title: Run low-cost wild bets first: handwritten notes and keep-it refunds
cards.summary: A staged rollout plan for unconventional retention plays, starting with handwritten notes to top customers and returnless refunds under $20.
cards.use_when: You want to test unscalable retention tactics on your store but need a low-cost, low-risk starting point before committing budget.

cards.title: Surprise-and-delight via personalized physical gestures (the Chewy play)
cards.summary: Use free personalized physical artifacts tied to an emotional hook to create shareable loyalty moments that big competitors can't replicate at scale.
cards.use_when: You sell in a category with an emotional anchor (pets, babies, homes, hobbies) and want to build customer-for-life loyalty without discounting.

cards.title: Empower support reps with a no-approval budget to recover and over-deliver
cards.summary: Give frontline staff a small discretionary budget to solve customer problems and add an unexpected touch, turning service recovery into a story customers retell.
cards.use_when: You want to reduce churn and turn problem moments into loyalty, or you're setting support policies for your store.

cards.title: Send handwritten notes and direct mail to repeat buyers
cards.summary: Use physical mail to cut through a full inbox and signal real effort, target proven repeat customers to control cost.
cards.use_when: You're designing a retention touch for repeat buyers or VIPs and want a measurable, non-discount incentive to reorder.

cards.title: Gate access with an invite-only or application model (the CRED play)
cards.summary: Restrict access to a tier, drop, or club to build desire through exclusivity rather than discounts.
cards.use_when: You're launching a new product tier, early drop, or loyalty club and want to build desire without cutting price.

cards.title: Build a VIP club for your top 1% of customers
cards.summary: Hand-pick your best buyers into an invitation-only tier and reward non-purchase actions as well as spend.
cards.use_when: You have enough repeat customers to segment a top tier and want to increase AOV and retention among your best buyers without discounting.

cards.title: Offer a lifetime warranty or repair-for-life on durable SKUs
cards.summary: Use radical guarantees to signal quality and remove the 'will it last?' objection, starting with your most durable products only.
cards.use_when: You sell durable goods and want to convert hesitation-driven abandoners by reversing the longevity risk.

cards.title: Run keep-it refunds on low-value items to cut return costs and build trust
cards.summary: Refund the customer and let them keep low-value items to avoid reverse-logistics costs that can exceed the product's value.
cards.use_when: You process returns on low-price, fragile, perishable, or hard-to-resell items and want to reduce return-handling costs and customer friction.

cards.title: Write an outcome guarantee to move risk from buyer to seller
cards.summary: Promise a specific result and a clear remedy if it fails, which can lift sales while barely raising refunds according to Hormozi.
cards.use_when: You sell a product with a measurable outcome (supplements, tools, courses, services) and want a stronger offer than a standard refund.

cards.title: Do things that don't scale to recruit and retain early customers
cards.summary: Treat manual, high-touch effort as a marketing investment, not an operational cost, to create superfans and learn what to build.
cards.use_when: You're in an early or growth stage and deciding whether to invest in manual outreach, personal onboarding, or founder-led support.

cards.title: Hold subscriber prices flat to avoid the discount death spiral
cards.summary: Grandfather early or subscriber pricing for life as a loyalty signal instead of discounting during inflation or competition.
cards.use_when: You're considering a price increase or promotion and want a loyalty-preserving alternative to a discount campaign.

cards.title: Run an anti-consumption or anti-sales campaign built on real values
cards.summary: Use honesty and values, backed by real repair or resale programs, to build trust that outsells a hard push.
cards.use_when: You have genuine sustainability or quality credentials and want a differentiated acquisition creative strategy that earns earned media.

cards.title: Use limited drops on a predictable schedule to sell at full price
cards.summary: Release small batches on a set cadence to build hype without discounting, using SMS as the announcement channel.
cards.use_when: You want to launch new products or limited editions without discounting and build a habitual purchase cadence.

cards.title: Build a named owner community with rituals and status markers
cards.summary: Create a named tribe, local chapters, and status symbols so belonging makes switching socially costly.
cards.use_when: You sell a product with repeat or enthusiast usage and want to reduce churn and drive word-of-mouth through community.

cards.title: Run customer co-creation and submit-and-vote product pipelines
cards.summary: Let customers submit and vote on product designs to create ownership, generate product research, and earn advocacy.
cards.use_when: You want to source product ideas, increase engagement, and turn fans into advocates without a discount.

cards.title: Add a low-cost surprise insert to VIP and first orders
cards.summary: Include a small unexpected gift, sample, or sticker in orders to trigger reciprocity and repeat buying.
cards.use_when: You're designing unboxing and packaging inserts for first orders or VIP orders and want a low-cost retention lift.

cards.title: Ship a proof-in-the-box test to beat claims with evidence
cards.summary: Give customers a way to test your quality against rivals inside the first order so they become the judge.
cards.use_when: You sell a commodity where quality is hard to communicate and you're confident your product wins a head-to-head test.

cards.title: Run a tiered referral waitlist with product rewards, not cash
cards.summary: Gate a launch behind a referral waitlist with escalating product rewards and a live progress bar to gamify sharing.
cards.use_when: You're planning a launch or drop and want to build an email list through referrals without cash incentives that attract fraud.

cards.title: Plan a single brand-voice stunt per season and measure earned media
cards.summary: Use funny, absurd, or values-driven stunts that fit your brand voice to earn media at a fraction of paid ad cost.
cards.use_when: You have a distinct brand voice and want a big-swing acquisition play that earns coverage rather than buying reach.

cards.title: Reward non-purchase loyalty actions to build status without discounts
cards.summary: Design loyalty rewards around reviews, referrals, and event invites rather than money-off to protect margin and build status.
cards.use_when: You're designing or revising a loyalty or VIP program and want to reward engagement rather than spending alone.

cards.title: Use an anti-discount stance and replace sales with bundles or gifts
cards.summary: Avoid chronic discounting because it signals weakness and raises price sensitivity; substitute gift-with-purchase or bundles instead.
cards.use_when: You're planning a promotion and considering a price cut, or you want to reduce discount dependence in your merchandising calendar.

cards.title: Set up a named VIP channel with a direct founder line
cards.summary: Give top customers a direct channel to the founder and first access to drops to lock in your highest-value segment.
cards.use_when: You want to reduce churn and increase AOV among your best customers and are deciding what the top tier of your loyalty program should include.

cards.title: Build a daily-drop habit loop with a fast launch cadence
cards.summary: Launch new SKUs or bundles on a frequent, predictable cadence to give customers a reason to check your store daily.
cards.use_when: You have a fast supply chain or agile product development and want to build a daily or weekly visitation habit.

cards.title: Add personalized art and emotional touches tied to your category
cards.summary: Commission cheap custom art or send emotional gestures tied to the customer's life moment to create shareable stories.
cards.use_when: You sell in a category with an emotional anchor (pets, babies, homes, hobbies) and want surprise-and-delight moments that drive organic sharing.

cards.title: Empower reps to over-deliver when a customer has a problem or personal moment
cards.summary: Give frontline staff a no-approval budget to solve problems and add an unexpected touch, turning recovery moments into stories customers retell.
cards.use_when: You're setting support policies and want to reduce churn by turning problem or personal moments into loyalty stories.

cards.title: Diagnose whether your growth is a faucet or a brand
cards.summary: Use the faucet metaphor to judge if your store disappears when ad spend stops, then shift budget toward talk-worthy differentiation.
cards.use_when: Strategic planning when deciding how much of your budget to keep in paid acquisition versus building a differentiated brand asset.

cards.title: Scarcity drop model: build the brand before the first sale
cards.summary: Run fixed-time, genuinely limited releases after a long brand-building runway rather than using fake countdown timers.
cards.use_when: Product selection and launch planning for a premium or hero SKU where you want hype instead of discount-driven volume.

cards.title: Test useful editorial content beyond direct product promotion
cards.summary: Send customers to external stories and non-product content in your newsletter, then measure engaged vs ad-sourced customer LTV.
cards.use_when: Email/newsletter merchandising and retention planning when you want to build trust with an audience not currently in buying mode.

cards.title: Expiring loyalty coins as a conversion trigger
cards.summary: Award loyalty points that expire in about 60 days and use multi-channel expiry reminders to create return visits.
cards.use_when: Retention and replenishment design for an existing loyalty program that currently produces flat repeat purchase behavior.

cards.title: Guerrilla launch: go where your buyers already gather
cards.summary: Skip ads at launch and show up physically where your target customers are, with something tangible and shareable.
cards.use_when: Launch acquisition planning for a new product or brand when you have little budget and a defined physical audience.

cards.title: Evaluate an event-linked refund promotion before making a public promise
cards.summary: Treat event-linked refunds as an experimental offer with a funded maximum liability, not a guaranteed prediction-market hedge.
cards.use_when: Pricing and promotion design for a high-visibility sales event where you want a memorable offer without uncapped refund exposure.

cards.title: Programmatic direct mail as a lifecycle trigger
cards.summary: Trigger physical mail from the same behavioral signals as your emails to cut through inbox fatigue on high-value segments.
cards.use_when: Cart abandonment, win-back, or loyalty lifecycle design when email alone is saturating and you want a higher-cost, higher-attention channel.

cards.title: Reactivate lapsed buyers with a personalized physical letter
cards.summary: Test a personalized letter campaign against an email-only control for customers who haven't purchased in 6-12 months.
cards.use_when: Win-back and replenishment campaigns for lapsed customer segments where email open and click rates have decayed.

cards.title: A/B test direct mail like a digital channel
cards.summary: Apply testing and personalization discipline to physical mailers, including unique response tracking.
cards.use_when: Direct mail optimization when you already send physical pieces and want to improve ROI rather than keep guessing at creative.

cards.title: Gamified commerce: mystery bundles and blind boxes
cards.summary: Sell bundles where the exact contents are unknown, but guarantee a stated minimum value to protect trust.
cards.use_when: Merchandising and bundle design for clearance, seasonal kits, or inventory that is already profitable at a discount.

cards.title: Seasonal daily-reveal habit loop with midnight expiry
cards.summary: Gate one offer per day behind a calendar interface, expire it at midnight, and use the missed day to drive the next visit.
cards.use_when: Holiday or anniversary campaign design where you want daily return visits rather than a single sitewide promo.

cards.title: Delayed discounts: reward after the next purchase, with expiry
cards.summary: Give customers a reward they have already earned but can only redeem on a future order, with a deadline attached.
cards.use_when: Loyalty and replenishment design when you want repeat purchases without cutting the price of the current order.

cards.title: Flash sales that don't damage the brand
cards.summary: Run urgency-driven sales only for loyalty segments, instead of blanket sitewide discounts.
cards.use_when: Pricing and promotion decisions when you need a conversion push but fear training the whole list to wait for discounts.

cards.title: Mystery-first launch: anonymous posters then reveal
cards.summary: Build curiosity with unbranded physical or digital placements, then reveal the brand and message in phases.
cards.use_when: New brand or product launch when you have zero brand recognition but want attention before you spend on media.

cards.title: Native in-game placements that hand out real value
cards.summary: Put real products or discount codes inside games and communities your customers already inhabit, rather than interrupting them with ads.
cards.use_when: Acquisition creative and campaign planning when your audience spends leisure time in games, forums, or niche communities.

cards.title: Festival activation: solve a real attendee problem
cards.summary: Bring a service or truck to an event and relieve an actual pain point rather than pitching your catalog.
cards.use_when: Experiential marketing planning when you want brand affection from a defined physical audience.

cards.title: Own an underserved or taboo topic in your category
cards.summary: Address a topic competitors avoid, on the platform where that audience talks, and measure CPA against your other channels.
cards.use_when: Acquisition channel selection and content strategy when your category has an underserved audience and competitors avoid the subject.

cards.title: Crowdfunding or pre-order to validate demand before inventory
cards.summary: Use an audience plus a crowdfunding launch to prove demand and generate marketing before committing to stock.
cards.use_when: Product selection and inventory planning for a new SKU when you have an audience but don't want to carry unsold inventory risk.

cards.title: Build the digital experience that replaces in-store trust
cards.summary: Over-invest in education, photography, and transparency to sell a high-consideration product sight-unseen.
cards.use_when: PDP and landing page design for categories where customers must touch or see the product before buying.

cards.title: Community as co-creators: high-touch insider programs
cards.summary: Make your best customers insiders with events, early access, and input into products before automating anything.
cards.use_when: Retention and community strategy when you want customers who actively promote the brand, not just repeat buyers.

cards.title: Build community before product, and let feedback shape the catalog
cards.summary: Gather an audience first, ask what they want, and let the product emerge from those conversations.
cards.use_when: New product line or category entry where you can afford to test direction with an audience before committing to design and inventory.

cards.title: Run a no-ads week experiment to test organic dependence
cards.summary: Pause paid acquisition for a short window and measure what organic traffic, content, and personal outreach can carry.
cards.use_when: Acquisition strategy review when you suspect the business depends entirely on paid channels.

cards.title: Turn customers into co-creators through structured feedback
cards.summary: Create a visible feedback loop so customers see their input shaping the product.
cards.use_when: Product roadmap and retention planning for a marketplace or catalog where customer experience drives repeat purchase.

cards.title: Question category assumptions to find structural advantage
cards.summary: Look for beliefs everyone in your category accepts as true, then test whether they're actually wrong.
cards.use_when: Strategy and product selection when your category commoditizes and you need a structural cost or positioning edge.

cards.title: Creator-first commerce: let affiliates drive discovery
cards.summary: Build creator and affiliate relationships and make their content the primary discovery and conversion engine.
cards.use_when: Acquisition channel planning when you want third-party content to carry discovery rather than your own ads.

cards.title: TikTok-first international expansion without local infrastructure
cards.summary: Test new markets through a platform that handles logistics and payments, before committing to offices or distributors.
cards.use_when: International expansion planning when you want to validate demand abroad without fixed local costs.

cards.title: Make your benefit entertaining and culturally specific
cards.summary: Convert a functional product benefit into a jingle-led, shareable, culturally resonant format.
cards.use_when: Paid and organic creative strategy when your product benefit is utilitarian and forgettable.

cards.title: Publish lifestyle content and monetize with matching products
cards.summary: Define a worldview your brand represents, publish content expressing it, and curate products that embody it.
cards.use_when: Content strategy and category positioning when you want customers to come for the content and stay for the products.

cards.title: Position stores as community hubs and spotlight real people
cards.summary: Treat physical retail as a creative and community space, and reduce paid influencer activity in favour of authentic figures.
cards.use_when: Retail expansion and brand-building decisions when you want intrinsic community pull rather than rented attention.

cards.title: Align your offer with a cultural or political moment
cards.summary: Identify a moment your customers care about and build a curated offer that lets them act on that sentiment.
cards.use_when: Product selection and bundle design when a cultural shift drives customers toward local or values-aligned buying.

cards.title: Run livestream selling with timed drops and real-time bidding
cards.summary: Collapse the distance between content and checkout by selling live with limited-time listings and auctions.
cards.use_when: Merchandising and channel testing for products that benefit from demonstration, storytelling, or collector appeal.

cards.title: Use a mystery hook to break through campaign noise
cards.summary: Launch a teasing format with an unexplained premise, then reveal it as an ad for your sale or product.
cards.use_when: Campaign creative planning around a major promotion when standard announcement assets are being ignored.

cards.title: Shift from discount positioning to cultural relevance
cards.summary: Invest in visual identity and influencer-led storytelling so customers see you as a style source, not a discount channel.
cards.use_when: Brand positioning review when price competition is destroying margin and you want to compete on taste instead.

cards.title: Turn a small store into a community with events and social
cards.summary: Use social media and recurring events to transform a small online retailer into a community destination.
cards.use_when: Community and local marketing for a small store that can't outspend larger competitors.

cards.title: Establish community-driven product development for resale or marketplace models
cards.summary: Let customer experience feedback directly shape platform and product evolution, and make the changes visible.
cards.use_when: Retention and product roadmap decisions for second-hand, marketplace, or community-driven commerce.

cards.title: Design a Wild Bet by Breaking a Category Convention
cards.summary: A step-by-step playbook for turning a constraining category 'rule' into a differentiated, hedged ecommerce experiment.
cards.use_when: You want to design one deliberate, differentiating store initiative (drop, loyalty mechanic, community play, campaign) instead of another incremental tactic.

cards.title: The 'Doesn't Scale' Philosophy for Defensible Ecommerce Advantage
cards.summary: Tactics that resist easy scaling (manual effort, personalization, human touch) create differentiation because competitors can't commoditize them.
cards.use_when: You're deciding where to invest founder time versus automation in acquisition, onboarding, or early-customer experience.

cards.title: Five Low-Cost 'Doesn't Scale' Ecommerce Experiments
cards.summary: Concrete, cheap founder-led tests — from the 20-customers exercise to a no-ads week — designed to surface customer insight and referrals.
cards.use_when: You want to test unscalable, human-touch tactics in acquisition, retention, or product development without a big budget.

cards.title: Programmatic Direct Mail for Abandoned-Cart and Browse Retargeting
cards.summary: Bring the abandoned-cart reminder into the physical mail stream with personalized product imagery and frequency caps.
cards.use_when: You have high cart or browse abandonment on high-consideration products and want a retargeting channel beyond email and ads.

cards.title: Triggered Direct Mail Mapped to Ecommerce Journeys
cards.summary: Treat physical mail as a behavioral trigger inside existing automations — welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, win-back — with content tailored by cohort.
cards.use_when: You are mapping lifecycle automations (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, win-back) and want to decide where a physical mailer adds value.

cards.title: Direct Mail for Second Purchase and Membership Onboarding
cards.summary: Use personalized physical letters at two high-leverage moments: first-to-second purchase and new loyalty-club membership.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to move first-time buyers to a repeat purchase or how to onboard new loyalty/club members.

cards.title: Evaluate third-party audience data for an ecommerce direct-mail test
cards.summary: Assess audience relevance, data provenance and permitted use before a third-party acquisition mailing.
cards.use_when: You're planning acquisition or win-back against named competitors (e.g. meal-kit or subscription categories) and need targeting data.

cards.title: Reflect Brand Values in Direct Mail Materials
cards.summary: Make paper stock, printing and messaging consistent with sustainability or premium positioning so the physical mailer reinforces rather than contradicts the brand.
cards.use_when: Your brand positioning rests on sustainability or premium quality and you are planning a direct mail or direct-mail retargeting program.

cards.title: Personalized Direct Mail for High-Value B2B Proposals (Wholesale, Corporate Gifts, Trade)
cards.summary: Tightly defined target personas plus personalized direct mail inside a multi-touch ABM campaign for large accounts.
cards.use_when: You sell wholesale, corporate gifting, bulk or trade accounts where a single account is worth substantial revenue.

cards.title: Build a Sticky Buying Moment Around Culture, Not a Generic Sale
cards.summary: Ride a cultural or political moment your customers care about, and make acting on it easy with pre-curated bundles.
cards.use_when: You are planning seasonal merchandising, bundles, or a campaign and deciding whether a cultural moment is an authentic fit for your store.

cards.title: Automate Rule-Based Operations Before Chasing Wild Bets
cards.summary: Use AI to absorb repetitive customer service, outreach and content tasks so solo operators can spend judgment on the bets that matter.
cards.use_when: You are a small or solo ecommerce team deciding what to automate versus what to keep manual.

cards.title: Scarcity, Clout and Exclusive Drops: Borrowing Streetwear Mechanics
cards.summary: Design product or campaign drops using scarcity and status so the release itself becomes the story.
cards.use_when: You are planning a product drop, limited release, or landing page for a new item and want it to spread without paid ads.

cards.title: Calculate true gross margin with the "all in until it's in" COGS rule
cards.summary: Define COGS as every cost incurred to get a product onto the warehouse shelf ready to sell, so gross margin reflects reality rather than guesswork.
cards.use_when: When setting product prices, deciding which sales channels to sell on, or reviewing whether a SKU is actually profitable.

cards.title: Sort each expense into COGS or operating expense before reporting margin
cards.summary: Use a consistent above-the-line/below-the-line split so gross profit comparisons across periods and channels mean something.
cards.use_when: When preparing monthly management accounts, evaluating channel profitability (Amazon vs Shopify), or diagnosing why profit does not match sales growth.
